text.title: sql-optimization Worked Examples
text.summary: One full end-to-end example of sql-optimization applied to a representative input, plus a narrated pass and a counter-example.

section.title: Worked example
section.p: Inputs match the artefacts listed in the AGENTS.md Prerequisites table; the output below conforms to 02-output-contract.xml and would pass scripts/validate-sql-optimization.py.

example.note: The valid example reflects a 96.7% p95 improvement from a single composite index addition.

example.title: Orders list slow query optimisation
example.note: query_id=slow_orders_list_v3. Baseline: Seq Scan on orders, estimated=10 000 against actual=1 500 000, 8 200 ms over sample=50. Investigation: the 150x estimate skew tripped investigate-row-estimate-skew, so ANALYZE orders ran first and the estimate corrected — only then was an index worth designing. Change: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ix_orders_tenant_created_id ON orders (tenant_id, created_at DESC, id), equality column first. After: Index Scan, actual_rows=100, 200 ms. wall_clock_delta_ms=-8000 over the same sample=50. The PR shipped with both plans attached; APM confirmed p95 fell from 8.5 s to 0.22 s.

example.title: Index by vibes
example.note: An engineer added six indexes "just in case" before capturing any plan. pg_stat_user_indexes showed one of the six ever used; write latency on the table had tripled. The tree catches this at the first branch — explain-before-change halts until a baseline exists — and the remediation was to collect the plans, keep the one index they justified, and drop the other five.
